evidence: Wikipedia's article on 'Bitches Brew': Thom Yorke cited it as an influence on 'OK Computer' (1997), describing it as building something up and watching it fall apart, and saying that was at the core of what the band were trying to do.

trackPair.whatToListenFor: Neither record has a simple shape. 'Bitches Brew' builds, falls apart and rebuilds over twenty minutes; 'Paranoid Android' goes through four sections in just over six minutes, from quiet acoustic to a violent guitar break to a slow choral passage and back. Listen for the moment each one seems about to collapse, and what happens next.

explanation: Thom Yorke said Miles Davis's 'Bitches Brew' was at the centre of what Radiohead were trying to do on 'OK Computer': build something up and watch it fall apart. A jazz-rock record from 1970 was named as the heart of a British guitar album 27 years later. The influence is on how it is built, not how it sounds: there is no trumpet on 'OK Computer'.
